title: Chapter 14 — Dishwashers
intro: Decibels, rack systems, wash performance, and the installation realities that make or break the sale.

sections.title: Decibels Matter More Than Customers Realize
sections.content:
Noise level is one of the biggest differentiators in dishwashers — and one of the easiest to demonstrate. The difference between 50 dB and 39 dB is the difference between hearing the dishwasher from the living room and forgetting it is running.

Use decibel comparisons in your demo. Relate the numbers to real life. 'At 42 decibels, this is quieter than a library.'

sections.title: Rack Systems and Capacity
sections.content:
Third-rack dishwashers are the standard in mid-range and above. The third rack creates space for utensils and small items, freeing up capacity in the lower racks.

Adjustable tines, fold-down shelves, and rack height adjustment all affect real-world usability. Show these features physically during the demo — they are tangible benefits customers can see and touch.

sections.title: Installation Realities
sections.content:
Dishwashers have specific requirements: water line, drain, electrical, and cabinet opening dimensions. Panel-ready models require custom panels that add cost and lead time.

Confirm installation details before closing. A dishwasher that does not fit the opening or requires electrical work the customer did not expect creates friction after the sale.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating dishwasher knowledge, ask:

Can the salesperson explain decibel ratings in relatable terms?
Do they demonstrate rack features physically?
Do they verify installation requirements before closing?
Do they present dishwashers as part of a kitchen package when appropriate?
